goals.detail:
### Queued: the hero walks onto a floor square holding more than one object

Set aside on 31 July 2026 when `scripts/scan-debt.mjs` landed. The scan rates
this behavior 383 screens of `supports` and 61 of `unlocks` in one session,
`seed0004-feeding-pony`, against 188 for `#levelchange`. Slice 1 was drafted and
never validated; that draft is parked on the branch `wip/object-pile-window` and
no line of it is verified against the C source.

A walking hero steps onto a square holding two or more objects with
`!autopickup`. `pickup.c pickup()` takes its `(autopickup && !flags.pickup)`
early return into `check_here(FALSE)`, the run stops, and `invent.c
look_here()` opens the `Things that are here:` window.

In scope: the `look_here()` branches reachable when the square holds more than
one object and no guard requiring `Blind`, `u.uswallow`, `is_pool`/`is_lava`,
`visible_region_at()`, a seen trap, `will_feel_cockatrice()` or a nonzero
`dfeature_at()` holds -- the `otmp->nexthere` window (`invent.c:4288-4313`) and
the `skip_objects` count line (`4251-4276`) that `flags.pile_limit` selects --
plus `pickup()`'s no-autopickup arm and its `nomul(0)` run stop. Excluded:
`autopick()` and `pickup_object()`, the whole autopickup arm.

`invent.c look_here()` (4104-4315) is already ported apart from those two
branches, and `js/pickup.js check_here()` is live at `js/hack.js:1158` behind
`domove_core()`, so the consumer exists. The work is widening
`requireSimpleHeroDestination()` (`js/hack.js:414-444`) and finishing
`look_here()`'s `'the object-pile menu'` throw at `js/invent.js:454`. Roughly
150 new C lines, two or three slices.

**Why it was selected, and what replaced that reasoning.** Over 60 freshly
generated D:1 levels (seeds 7100000-7100059) the port produces 19.4 squares
holding an object per level, in 100% of levels, and 1.28 squares holding a
*pile*, in 72%, against 1.12 traps, 0.75 fountains and 0.10 sinks. Object
squares outnumber every other unported destination class by an order of
magnitude, and 20 of 33 development sessions set `!autopickup`. That argument
measured incidence on a generated level, which no development session samples.
`scripts/scan-debt.mjs` measures the recorded sessions themselves and reaches a
different answer: one session needs this owner, and it earns 61 screens there.

`seed0004-feeding-pony` stops here at 26 of 409 steps.

**The `flush_screen()` question, traced but not yet recorded.** Whether the
pile window trips the menu-erasure defect under `## Unresolved` was left open
when this goal was queued. A source trace says it does not. `pline.c:274`'s
`if (u.ux) flush_screen()` is the only such call inside `vpline()`, and between
`create_nhwindow()` and `destroy_nhwindow()` at `invent.c:4288-4313` there is
no `pline()`, `You()` or `There()` -- only `putstr()`, `doname_with_price()`
and `display_nhwindow()`. `check_here()`'s own `flush_screen(1)`
(`pickup.c:451`) runs before the window opens. The one message that can follow
is `read_engr_at()`'s, after `destroy_nhwindow()` has already repaired the
corner through `docorner()`, and `js/hack.js:453` refuses an engraving on an
admitted square regardless. The defect's two known victims are menu *search*
prompts, which a window with no menu items cannot reach. That is a trace, not
evidence; slice 1's differential converts it, and converts it automatically,
because a wrong reading shows up as a mismatched pile screen.

**Slices.**

1. *The window itself.* A walking hero's one-square step onto a ROOM or CORR
   square holding two to four objects, ending at the dismissed
   `Things that are here:` window and the next command prompt. Upstream:
   `look_here()`'s final `else` arm (`invent.c:4288-4313`) and its tty
   realization -- `wintty.c tty_putstr()`'s NHW_MENU case (2360-2410, with
   `compress_str()` and the `n0 > CO` line break), `tty_display_nhwindow()`'s
   NHW_MENU arm, `dmore()`, and `tty_dismiss_nhwindow()` into
   `erase_menu_or_text()`'s `docorner(offx, maxrow + 1, 0)`.
2. *The count line.* `skip_objects` at `invent.c:4251-4276`
   (`There are two/a few/several/many objects here.`), which `flags.pile_limit`
   selects, plus explicit non-default settings including `pile_limit:0` and
   `pile_limit:1`. Message only; no window, and none of slice 1's rendering.
3. *A pile on a decorated square.* Lifting `js/hack.js:445`'s
   `terrain feature description` refusal for a staircase or doorway holding a
   pile, which adds the `dfeature` header `putstr()` pair at 4291-4294 and its
   blank separator. This merges with the separately listed hero-destination
   stop for a decorated square holding an object, whose `dfeature_at()` and
   `stairs_description()` are ported already.

The count line is second rather than first because the default `pile_limit` is
5: an ordinary walk meets a two-to-four pile, and a pile of five or more is the
rarer case that "complete common gameplay first" defers.

**Where slice 1's difficulty sits: rendering, not game logic.** Three traced
hazards, recorded here because each is invisible until it is fatal.
`tty_display_nhwindow()` routes this NHW_MENU to `process_text_window()`
because `cw->data` is non-NULL, while still using *menu* geometry --
`offx = max(10, cols - maxcol - 1)`, `offy = 0`, `dmore()` offset 2 and the
`(end)` prompt -- so neither `renderTtyMenu()` nor `displayTtyTextWindow()` is
the right donor alone; the port needs the first one's layout and the second
one's line loop. `maxcol` is `strlen(str) + 1` after `compress_str()`,
maximized over every line including the heading, and one character off shifts
the window a column and misses every cell in it, discontinuously, because
`offx === 10` flips to a full-screen clear. And `tty_putstr()` splits a line
wider than `CO` at the last space before column 79 and re-submits it, adding a
row and changing `maxcol`, before `display_nhwindow()` computes any layout.
`js/tty_menu.js:340` `displayTtyTextWindow()` hardcodes `offx = 0`;
`dismissTtyMenu()` (`js/tty_menu.js:278-311`) already models the
`maxrow + 1` repair that erases the `(end)` row, and is the better donor for
it. `display_nhwindow(WIN_MESSAGE, FALSE)`'s
`toplin == TOPLINE_NEED_MORE -> more()` arm has no owner in the port at all.

goals.detail:
### The hero's experience level rises

**The bounding property, testable against the C source.** C code is in scope
exactly when it runs while `u.ulevel` increases and is reached from
`wizcmds.c wiz_level_change()`'s `newlevel > u.ulevel` arm or from
`exper.c newexplevel()`. Code that runs only while `u.ulevel` decreases is out:
`exper.c losexp()` (207-297) and `wiz_level_change()`'s `newlevel < u.ulevel`
arm stay fail-closed. No recorded session lowers a level.

**What the goal gates.** A capped ceiling of 128 recorded steps across the five
sessions stopped on `#levelchange`; `scan-debt` rates the same owner 1,785
screens of `supports` across those five. All five sessions' next unmet command
after the stretch is `wizlevelport` (`^V`), so this goal opens the wizard-mode
level-teleport sequence for a later goal. It also deletes the `goto_level() as a
Tourist reaching a new level` refusal at `js/do.js:661`, which stands in front of
the Tourist descents in `seed0900`, `seed5006` and `seed0030`'s second life.

**Upstream owners and how much C.** `wizcmds.c wiz_level_change()` 444-486 (43
lines); `exper.c pluslvl()` 305-376 (72), `more_experienced()` 167-201 (35),
`newexplevel()` 298-305 (8); `attrib.c` innate tables 23-105 (83 lines of data),
`adjabil()` 1004-1073 (70), `role_abil()` 787-816 (30), `postadjabil()` 778-787
(10), `setuhpmax()` 1155-1177 (23); `botl.c xlev_to_rank()` 296-310,
`rank_to_xlev()` 313-330, `exp_percentage()` 2050-2083 and
`exp_percent_changing()` 2088-2124 (mostly `STATUS_HILITES`-gated and
unreachable); `weapon.c add_weapon_skill()` 1435-1451, `give_may_advance_msg()`
74-86; `insight.c record_achievement()` 2405-2472, `count_achievements()`
2492-2501, `achieve_rank()` 2504-2512. Roughly 380 live C lines plus the 83-line
table.

**What the port already has.** `exper.c newuexp()` and `newpw()` are ported in
`js/exper.js`; `attrib.c newhp()` at `js/attrib.js:99`; `weapon.c can_advance()`
and `slots_required()` at `js/weapon.js:841-863`; `display.c see_monsters()`,
which `postadjabil()` calls for `HWarning` and `HSee_invisible`, at
`js/display.js:1833`; `dungeon.c level_difficulty()`; and `tty_getlin()` at
`js/getline.js:328`, so the `To what experience level do you want to be set?`
prompt has an owner. `js/extcmdlist_data.js:81` already holds the `levelchange`
row with `WIZMODECMD`, and `js/cmd.js:212` and `:1105` already gate wizard-mode
rows, so the only missing wiring is a `case 'wiz_level_change'` in the dispatch
switch at `js/cmd.js:1138-1165`. `u.ulevelmax`, `u.ulevelpeak`, `u.uhppeak` and
`u.uenpeak` all exist in `js/u_init.js`.

**Traced findings that shape the work.**

- `pluslvl()`'s `Upolyd` arm (`monhp_per_lvl()`, `setmhmax`) is unreachable:
  `js/u_init.js` is the port's only writer of `u.umonnum` and sets it equal to
  `u.umonster`.
- `pluslvl()`'s `Welcome back to experience level %d.` arm is unreachable on a
  rising path: `u.ulevelmax` is bumped inside the same block, so every recorded
  line reads `Welcome to experience level N.`
- Message order is load-bearing for the random-number log.
  `You_feel("more experienced.")` prints before `newhp()` and `newpw()` consume
  `rnd()`/`rn1()`, `++u.ulevel` and the `Welcome` pline follow, and `adjabil()`
  runs last. The recorded streams confirm it: at level 15 `seed0360` reads
  `You feel sensitive!  You feel more experienced.--More--`, the intrinsic line
  trailing level 15's welcome and sharing a top line with level 16's opening.
- `add_weapon_skill()` prints nothing in any of the five sessions because
  `can_advance()` also requires
  `P_ADVANCE(skill) >= practice_needed_to_advance(...)`, and a hero who has
  struck nothing has zero practice, so `before == after`. The slot increment is
  still real state.
- `livelog_printf()` writes a file the port cannot write and reaches no screen,
  matching the treatment already recorded at `js/do.js:658-660`.
- Rank achievements do fire: `xlev_to_rank(20)` is 5, so a 1-to-20 change records
  `ACH_RNK1` through `ACH_RNK5` into `u.uachieved[]`. No screen output, but it is
  saved state.
- Hazard: `postadjabil()` calls `see_monsters()` when `HWarning` or
  `HSee_invisible` changes -- levels 15 (Wizard, Priest, Caveman, Healer), 7 and
  15 (Monk), and 15 (Ranger). `js/display.js:1852` and `:1864` throw on a long
  worm and on a warning artifact, neither of which these levels hold, but the
  warning-glyph path through `newsym()` is untested, and that file's header
  comment saying no level change is ported goes stale with this goal.

**Indicative slices** (the slice-selector decides the real division).

1. *The command and one level gain.* `wiz_level_change()`'s prompt, parse, and
   its equal and raising arms; `pluslvl()` with `setuhpmax()`; the welcome line
   and the status line. `adjabil()` and the lowering arm stay fail-closed.
2. *The intrinsics a level grants.* The innate tables, `adjabil()`,
   `role_abil()`, `postadjabil()`, `add_weapon_skill()`.
3. *Rank achievements.* `record_achievement()`, `count_achievements()`,
   `achieve_rank()`, `rank_to_xlev()`.
4. *Experience points from play.* `more_experienced()`, `newexplevel()`,
   `exp_percent_changing()`, wired to the Tourist arm at `js/do.js:661`, deleting
   that refusal.

**Why this goal and not the queued pile window.** Re-ranked at `af2b7335` by the
capped look-ahead forecast `.agents/selection.md` requires. Six candidates were
capped with `scripts/scan-ahead.mjs` and a classifier holding the port's boundary
and command sets: `#levelchange` 128 (5 sessions, no stretch cut), pet ranged
targeting 33 of a raw 370 (4 sessions, an eleven-fold cut on combat, a trap and a
count prefix), door or special terrain movement 31 (3, uncut), `#twoweapon` 21 of
35, movement while riding 10 of 31, and the floor object pile 1 of 61. Hero or
monster combat caps four of the six; `#levelchange` is the only candidate whose
stretches hold no second unported behavior, so nothing has to be priced in. It
wins on both ranking keys -- highest capped forecast and most sessions stopped --
so no tie-break applies.

goals.detail:
### The hero enters a furniture square

`rm.h:138` defines `IS_FURNITURE(typ)` as `typ >= STAIRS && typ <= ALTAR`, which
is this goal's whole subject: stairs, ladders, thrones, fountains, sinks, graves
and altars. The hero reaches one by walking, by running, or by swapping with the
ordinary starting pet standing on it.

**The stop is measured, not inferred.** Replaying each session and catching the
boundary with `onBoundary` on `runSegment()` puts the two `seed0013` sessions at
`js/hack.js:627` inside `requireSimpleHeroDestination()`, hero at (34,15),
refused destination (35,15), `typ=30` = `SINK` (`js/const.js:77`), with
`context.run === 1`. `seed2600` stops at `js/hack.js:885` inside
`requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap()`, refused destination (60,3), `typ=26` =
`STAIRS`, occupied by the kitten. One census row, two seams, two terrains. C's
recorded screen confirms the sink: the hero stands on the `{` at the next step
with an empty top line.

**C reaches almost nothing new, which is why the refusal is the whole cost.**
`hack.c test_move()`'s chain has no arm for furniture -- `IS_OBSTRUCTED` is
`typ < POOL` (`rm.h:119`) and `IS_DOOR` is false -- so an orthogonal step falls
through to `testdiag` and is admitted. The run stop at `hack.c:2936-2941`
(`IS_DOOR || IS_OBSTRUCTED || IS_FURNITURE(tmpr->typ)`) is already ported at
`js/hack.js:1461-1466`. `hack.c spoteffects()` (3312-3480) has exactly one
furniture arm, `IS_SINK(...) && Levitation -> dosinkfall()` at 3353-3354,
unreachable without levitation; its tail below the `pickup(1)` at 3381 holds only
the ice warning and the hidden-monster surprise, both refused ahead of it.
`pickup.c:702-709` returns before `look_here()` on an object-free square, running
`describe_decor()` only under `flags.mention_decor` and then `read_engr_at()`.

**Where the work actually sits.** Two sibling guards are written against
`STAIRS || doorway` and must be restated against the same predicate, or widening
`ordinaryDestination` silently admits cases they were holding: `js/hack.js:636-639`
(`'decor description'`) and `js/hack.js:653-656` (`'terrain feature
description'`). `invent.c dfeature_at()` is already ported (`js/invent.js:161-230`)
and covers fountain, throne, sink and grave through the cmap; its ALTAR arm throws
for `a_gname()` and its ice arm for `ice_descr()`, so ALTAR needs those helpers or
an explicit refusal. A temple altar is already bounded: `js/rooms.js` refuses
`check_special_room()` entering room type TEMPLE.

**The pet swap has no terrain condition in C.** `hack.c domove_swap_with_pet()`
(2098-2180) tests the pet's trapped state, its diagonal ability, a boulder on the
hero's square, `bad_rock()`, and `goodpos(u.ux0, u.uy0, mtmp, 0)` for the square
the *pet* moves into. It never tests the square the hero moves onto.
`js/hack.js:879-888`'s ROOM/CORR/D_NODOOR list is a seam artifact that lags the
walk seam, which already admits STAIRS.

**Incidence, as context and explicitly not as a forecast.** Over 80 freshly
generated D:1 levels (seeds 7300000-7300079, Valkyrie, datetime 20290418073000)
the port's own generator produces 1.09 non-stairs furniture squares per level,
with 68% of levels holding at least one: fountains 0.80, sinks 0.15, altars 0.07,
graves 0.06, and no thrones or ladders on D:1. `docs/goal-history.md` demotes
fresh incidence to nomination only, and records that the pet-inventory goal was
chosen on fresh incidence alone and returned a holdout zero. It is here only to
say which terrain the first slice should cover -- the fountain -- and that ladder
and throne belong last or stay refused.

**Why this goal and not the field.** Capped look-ahead on 2 August 2026 across
twelve candidates: this boundary 31 (3 sessions, no stretch cut), `apply` 26 (2),
`#twoweapon` 24 of 35 (1), `#pray` 21 (1), pet ranged targeting 20 of 370 (4),
`fire` 17 (1), monster trap activation 16 (1), `wizlevelport` 14 of 95 (4),
`takeoff` 14 (2), movement while riding 10 of 31 (1), and the floor object pile 1
of 61 (1). Pet ranged targeting stops the most sessions but its four stretches cap
on four different unported behaviors -- graffiti, `#ride`, hero combat and a count
prefix -- so its sessions buy the shallowest follow-on in the field.

**Indicative slices** (the slice-selector decides the real division).

1. *The walk onto a bare fountain or sink.* Widen the seam to `IS_FURNITURE()`
   and restate the two sibling guards. Closes on both `seed0013` sessions plus a
   fresh differential over a fountain and a sink.
2. *The ordinary-pet swap onto furniture.* Closes on `seed2600`.
3. *Grave and altar.* Includes `dfeature_at()`'s `a_gname()` arm or its explicit
   refusal, with the case just outside the limit being an altar inside a temple.

goals.detail:
### Clearing the `commands` deferral backlog

`npm run quality -- deferrals` reports `commands` holding ten open entries
outside the `scope` category, which is the threshold `.agents/selection.md`
sets for a deferred-area sweep. A sweep takes precedence over any fail-closed
boundary port until the area drops below it, and each open entry is already a
slice, scoped when it was deferred, so this goal needs no slice selection.

The ten, as at `e3a3d1d`:

1. `the status line repaints on every turn, where C gates it` (production)
2. `u_on_newpos() drops earth_sense() with no refusal` (production)
3. `a drawbridge wall answers "It's a wall."` (production)
4. `three arms of the door message switch are dormant` (production)
5. `the m prefix loses a frame` (production)
6. `go.occupation has one writer and three readers that never see it`
   (production)
7. `movement-path-has-no-failclosed-wrapper` (production, slice)
8. `eight diagonal-doorway findings are deferred` (clarity)
9. `the two-meal segment never reaches its second meal` (tests)
10. `adjabil()'s already-held suppression test has no reachable case` (tests,
    slice, and blocked on `#wizintrinsic`)

**Order.** Two of the ten are fail-open rather than fail-closed, meaning the
port skips a message-writing C branch silently instead of stopping: entries 1
and 2. `AGENTS.md` singles that out as the one thing an unported path must not
do, so they come first. Entry 1 leads because it sits on a line that runs every
turn of every session and its own record calls it the first
emitted-and-wrong screen the project would produce; entry 2's branch is dormant
for a narrower reason that is now written down, that every burial site on a
reachable level is a GRAVE or STONE square which `earth_sense()` rejects before
reading the buried list.

Entry 10 cannot close inside this goal: it waits on `#wizintrinsic`, which no
goal has ported. It stays open and the area stays at nine until then, which is
below the threshold.

**What a sweep is worth.** Nothing in recorded steps, by construction: every
entry names behavior no development session reaches, which is why each was
deferred rather than fixed. The forecast is recorded as 0 for that reason, not
as a guess. Entry 1 is the exception in one direction -- it changes rendering
on a line every turn draws, so it can move the score either way and needs its
own differential and a whole-score comparison rather than an audit-fix line.

forecast.basis: capped look-ahead, 2 August 2026, over the two sessions the wish stops: seed0360-wizard-world-tour 90 of 90 and seed0108-wizard-extcmd-wishlist 16 of 16, neither cut. Step-level streams hold only the tty_getlin echo and the result line, and the recorded random-number log across all four wishes names only rnd_otyp_by_namedesc, next_ident, mksobj_init, blessorcurse and makewish's rn1(100,50). Highest of eight candidates; pet ranged targeting caps at 36 of 373 over five sessions. Note that 90 of the 106 are the getlin echo, whose owner is already ported.

goals.detail:
### A wizard-mode hero wishes for an object

**The bounding property, testable against the C source.** The wish text reaches
`readobjnam_postparse3()`'s `rnd_otyp_by_namedesc(d->actualn, d->oclass, 1)`
(`objnam.c:4749-4759`) and matches exactly one `objects[]` entry, after
`readobjnam_preparse()` consumed only a count, a `blessed`/`cursed`/`uncursed`
word and a `+N`/`-N` enchantment, and `readobjnam_postparse1()` consumed only a
class word. The created object is not an artifact, corpse, statue, figurine,
egg, tin, glob, fruit or container; the hero has a free inventory slot and is
not `Fumbling`, so `hold_another_object()` takes its plain `addinv` tail.

**Read the forecast correctly.** 106 capped steps across two sessions, both
uncapped, but 90 of them are `seed0360`'s `tty_getlin()` echo, and
`tty_getlin()` is already ported at `js/getline.js:328`. The goal unlocks a long
stretch of replay for a modest amount of new behavior. That is a good trade and
not a large-behavior forecast; judge the delivered figure against it knowing
where the steps come from.

**Upstream and how much C.** 1,854 lines by exact span: `wizcmds.c wiz_wish()`
32-44; `zap.c makewish()` 6314-6422; `objnam.c readobjnam()` 4910-5400,
`readobjnam_init()` 3933-3961, `readobjnam_preparse()` 3966-4175,
`readobjnam_parse_charges()` 4178-4237, `readobjnam_postparse1()` 4240-4663,
`readobjnam_postparse2()` 4666-4724, `readobjnam_postparse3()` 4727-4899,
`wishymatch()` 3243-3338, `rnd_otyp_by_namedesc()` 3455-3529;
`invent.c hold_another_object()` 1208-1306 and `prinv()` 2875-2890. Most is
refused rather than ported. The in-scope path is the `preparse` qualifier arms,
`postparse1`'s class-word extraction, `postparse2`'s `makesingular`,
`postparse3`'s four `rnd_otyp_by_namedesc()` calls, and `readobjnam()`'s
`typfnd:` tail. This goal needs a checklist under `AGENTS.md` and closes over
several slices.

**What the port already has.** `tty_getlin()` (`js/getline.js:328`); `mksobj()`
(`js/obj.js:1451`), `mksobj_init()` (`js/obj.js:1191`), `blessorcurse()` and
`next_ident()`; `addinv()` (`js/invent.js:1850`); `donameFresh()`
(`js/objnam.js:773`); `mungspaces()`; `encumber_msg()`; and the `objects[]` and
`obj_descr[]` tables. Missing entirely: `readobjnam` and its chain,
`wishymatch`, `rnd_otyp_by_namedesc`, `hold_another_object`, `prinv`,
`makewish`, `wiz_wish`.

**Traced findings.**

- The wish-history machinery is dead in the comparison build.
  `wish_history_add()`, `wish_history_menu()` and `wish_history_flush()` are each
  inside `#ifdef DEBUG` (`zap.c:6229`, 6261, 6277), and `config.h` defines only
  `DEBUG_MIGRATING_MONS` at 620, with no patch under `nethack-c/patches/`
  defining `DEBUG`. So `wish_history[0]` is always NULL and `makewish()`'s

goals.detail:
### A wizard-mode hero teleports to a numbered dungeon level

**The bounding property, testable against the C source.** `wiz_level_tele()`
runs with `wizard` set; `level_tele()` takes the
`(Teleport_control && !Stunned) || wizard` arm; `getlin()`'s answer is a decimal
string for which `lev_by_name()` returns 0 and `atoi()` a positive `newlev`;
`single_level_branch(&u.uz)` and `In_quest(&u.uz)` are false and `next_to_u()`
is true; `get_level()` resolves `newlev` inside dnum 0 to a level whose
`level_info[].flags` lacks `LFILE_EXISTS`; and `goto_level()` runs with
`at_stairs`, `falling` and `portal` all FALSE, reaching `u_on_rndspot(0)`.

**Out of scope.** The `?` menu (`print_dungeon()`), `*` and the
`random_levtport` arm, negative levels with their heaven, Nowhere and `done()`
paths, the `In_endgame` arm, the non-wizard `Teleport_control` route,
`level_tele_trap()` and `mlevel_tele_trap()`, and any destination that is a
special level or one already generated.

**Read the forecast correctly.** 180 capped steps, and 174 of them are the
already-ported `getlin()` echo and wish-result lines. The six genuinely new
screens are the prompt, its echo and the arrival in each of the two sessions.
The forecast therefore rests on the just-closed wish path holding across four
object classes it did not exercise: wand, ring, scroll, and tool or container. A
divergence in any one wish truncates the rest of that session, so judge the
delivered figure knowing that most of it is replay the goal unlocks rather than
behavior it adds.

**Upstream and how much C.** About 550 lines read, roughly 230 of them in-scope
arms to translate, which is comparable to the descent goal and smaller than
`wizard-mode-wish`'s parser. `wizcmds.c wiz_level_tele()` 399-406;
`teleport.c level_tele()` 1164-1440, the wizard positive-number arm only;
`do.c schedule_goto()`, `deferred_goto()` and `goto_level()`'s `!at_stairs` arm
1802-1810; `dungeon.c get_level()`, `lev_by_name()`, `single_level_branch()` and
`u_on_rndspot()` 1604-1638; `mkmaze.c place_lregion()`, `put_lregion_here()`,
`bad_location()` and `is_exclusion_zone()`; `mklev.c occupied()` 1806-1812; and
`allmain.c moveloop_core()` 538-539.

**Traced findings.**

- `js/do.js goto_level()` is the descent port, and the arrival arm this goal
  needs is one refusal to lift: `js/do.js:540-544` throws
  `'goto_level() arriving without stairs'`. The `up` refusal at 545-550 does not
  fire, because both destinations are below D:1.
- A prerequisite rather than a widening. `js/mklev.js:200-238` already carries
  `place_lregion()` and `bad_location()`, both commented "simplified for
  skeleton". `bad_location()` omits C's `occupied()` (`mklev.c:1806`) and the
  `AIR` term, and `put_lregion_here()` is absent altogether. The `LR_DOWNTELE`
  arm is what a level teleport uses, and it relocates a monster standing on the
  chosen square through `rloc(mtmp, RLOC_NOMSG)` and `m_into_limbo()`, but only
  on the deterministic pass; the probabilistic pass retries instead, spending
  two `rn1()` calls per try. The existing helper is wrong for this caller as
  written.
- `next_to_u()` is ported at `js/apply_next_to_u.js` and answers TRUE for an
  ordinary hero with a pet, so `level_tele()`'s `You1(shudder_for_moment)` guard
  passes without new work.
- `schedule_goto()` and `deferred_goto()` have no port. `js/allmain.js:777`
  already refuses the other call site, `allmain.c:385-386` inside the monster
  loop; the one this goal needs is `allmain.c:538-539`, after `rhack()`.
  `wiz_level_tele()` returns `ECMD_OK`, so no time passes and no monster moves
  between the command and the arrival: the whole transition happens inside one
  keystroke.
- `dungeon.c get_level()`, `lev_by_name()` and `single_level_branch()` are
  absent from `js/dungeon.js`. For a numeric answer `lev_by_name()` runs only
  its `find_mapseen_by_str()` leg, the port keeping no mapseen chain per
  `js/do.js:454-459`, then `find_level()` (ported at `js/dungeon.js:803`) and
  `find_branch()`, and returns 0, so `atoi()` supplies `newlev`.
- Both destinations are ordinary levels, measured rather than assumed. Booting
  the port for each seed and reading `game.dungeon_topology`: seed5002 places the
  Oracle at D:8, the Mines branch at D:4 and Sokoban at D:9, so D:5 carries no
  special map and no branch; seed5006 places its Mines branch on D:2, the level
  it teleports to, so `place_branch()` (`js/mklev.js:3181`) runs on arrival. Both
  sit inside what the descent goal validated: 2,347 of 2,347 fresh descents
  reached a drawn D:2 (`docs/goal-history.md:34`,
  `scripts/run-leave-level.mjs`).
- The `?` menu is deliberately out of scope. It is `dungeon.c print_dungeon()`,
  three pages of branch and special-level rows including the castle tune. The
  only two sessions that use it spend the selection on a level `mklev()` cannot
  build, so including it buys 3 screens in seed0383 and 4 in seed0373 and then
  stops.
- The census hides a cap here, and it is a destination rather than a prompt.
  seed0383 is cut from 95 to 0 at step 42 and seed0373 from 85 to 0 at step 43:
  both answer the prompt with `?` and select a Lua special level, `e - bigrm: 12`
  and fakewiz1 at 46, that `mklev()` cannot build. seed0373's Amulet wish at
  steps 104-106, an unmodelled fifth route into `makewish()` through
  `allmain.c:445-449`, sits behind that arrival and never becomes the binding
  cap. The general caution stands: the debt model classifies commands, so a
  prompt-answering byte can hide an unported behavior.
- `js/wizcmds.js` already ports `wiz_wish()` and `wiz_level_change()`, so
  `wiz_level_tele()` belongs in that file, and `js/extcmdlist_data.js:167`
  already carries the `0x16 wizlevelport` row. The entry point is
  `ADMITTED_COMMANDS` at `js/cmd.js:711`, the list the current boundary message
  recites.

**Why this goal and not the field.** Capped look-ahead on 3 August across eleven
candidates: this boundary 180 over two sessions, pet ranged targeting 36 of 373
over five, `#twoweapon` 21 of 35, `apply` 21 of 26, movement while riding 10 of
31, the floor object pile 1 of 61, and fifteen others whose uncapped ceiling is
22 or less, which no capping read can raise above the runner-up. Pet ranged
targeting carries the highest raw figure and was set aside on arithmetic alone:
four separate unported behaviors sit inside its five stretches, cutting 373 to
36, which is below even the last closed goal's delivered 106. This goal was
preferred at five times that capped figure and because it opens a capability the
port wholly lacks, arriving on a level other than by walking down a staircase,
which `.agents/selection.md` names as the property that has moved the holdout.

**`object-pile-window` was re-ranked, not opened.** Its capped figure is 1 of 61,
in the single session seed0004-feeding-pony, and the census's 61 is a projection
of that one session's remaining input rather than a second measurement. Its
queued entry keeps its slice plan and `flush_screen()` trace, and sits behind
this goal.

**Calibration.** The three most recent non-sweep goals delivered 1.00, 0.90 and
1.00 of their capped forecasts, so 180 should be read as a genuine expectation
rather than the upper bound `unlocks` used to be.

goals.detail:
### Ordinary starting pets evaluate distant targets

The source-bounded capability is the target-selection pass reached from dog_move() for an active starting kitten, little dog, or pony. best_target() scans eight rays through find_targ() to distance 7 and score_targ() ranks a visible ordinary target. The three fixed starting species have only AT_BITE or AT_KICK followed by AT_NONE; score_targ() rejects adjacent targets. A selected target therefore reaches only mattackm()'s distant physical-attack miss path and the pet may continue moving. Real AT_WEAP, AT_BREA, or AT_SPIT attacks, special or confused pets, minions, priests, vampshifters, melee, retaliation, and displacement remain outside this goal and fail closed.

The current port already owns find_targ() in js/dogmove.js. The missing coherent group is dogmove.c find_friends(), score_targ(), best_target(), and pet_ranged_attk(), plus dog_move()'s call. Roughly 328 C lines define that targeting group. mhitm.c mattackm() is larger in full, but this boundary reaches only its setup and distant bite, kick, and AT_NONE miss projection. That narrow source-named port belongs in js/mhitm.js and must preserve source quirks even though the attack misses: wake a helpless target, set visibility, assign magr->mlstmv to moves, clear skipdrin, and return M_ATTK_MISS without a to-hit draw. mhitu.c getmattk() substitutions cannot fire for the three fixed species.

Fresh scan-sessions and look-ahead classification at c27653f cap the raw 394-step ceiling to 42 across five sessions: seed0030 contributes 15 before pet combat, seed0103 14 before pony combat, seed0200 6 before hero combat, seed0900 4 before pet combat, and seed2600 3 before the still-partial level-teleport question-mark route. One ambiguous byte inside those stretches is the already-supported #ride prompt. This boundary opens those later pet-combat, hero-combat, and print_dungeon boundaries without claiming them.

Runner-up apply carries 26 uncapped steps across two sessions, below 42 over five. The queued object-pile-window remains behind this goal because its raw 61-step stretch caps at 1: bear-trap activation follows the Things-that-are-here window immediately.

goals.detail:
### The hero applies a tool

`apply.c doapply()` (4214-4430) is the `a` command. Its entry is short — `nohands()`, `check_capacity()`, `getobj("use or apply", apply_ok, GETOBJ_NOFLAGS)`, `retouch_object()`, then three `oclass` shortcuts (wand, spellbook, coin) and a switch on `otyp`. Two arms of that switch carry the whole forecast: `STETHOSCOPE` at 4327-4329 and `LOCK_PICK` at 4290-4293. Everything else in the switch is the goal's boundary and must stop at a named refusal, including `SACK` reaching `use_container()`, which the Rogue also carries as inventory letter `f`.

**The stop is measured.** Both sessions stop on the port's repeated-command boundary refusing the byte `a` (`js/cmd.js:783-786`, `ADMITTED_COMMANDS` at 717-720). The scan puts `seed0016` at 3/36 and `seed0077` at 18/33, and both stretches were read step by step against the recorded keys, not from the top-line summary.

**Most of the scaffolding is already ported.** `getobj()` is `js/invent.js:369` and already serves `eat`, so `apply_ok()` plugs into an existing consumer rather than needing one. `getdir()` is `js/cmd.js:515`, `confdir()` is `js/cmd.js:496`, `check_capacity()` is `js/hack.js:255`, and `nohands()` is `js/mondata.js`. `js/lock.js` already owns `lock.c`'s `xlock` context, `reset_pick()` and `maybe_reset_pick()`, and its header comment names `pick_lock()` as the deliberate gap, so `pick_lock()` lands in the file that is already waiting for it.

**Three things are genuinely new.** `insight.c ustatusline()` (3402) has no port; `js/insight.js` is its owner. `freehand()` has no port and gates `use_stethoscope()`'s third guard. `svc.context.stethoscope_seq` compared against `gh.hero_seq` (decl.c:394, allmain.c:260 and 396) is the free-action rule that decides whether the first stethoscope use of a move costs time; `state.hero_seq` already exists (`js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js:237`, validated at `js/allmain.js:428`), so only the `stethoscope_seq` half is missing, and it needs one owner.

**`retouch_object()` needs a decision before the first commit.** `js/eat.js` references it but `js/` has no port; `QUALITY.json` carries `artifactTouchable() crashes a segment instead of ending it` against the same area. Neither starting kit holds an artifact, so the branch is dormant for both sessions, but it sits between `getobj()` and the switch and must be ported or refused explicitly rather than skipped.

**A branch neither starting character reaches.** `use_stethoscope()`'s `u.usteed`, `u.uswallow`, `u.dz` and cursed-object arms (346-378) are all unreachable here: `.` zeroes all three deltas and both stethoscopes are `{ STETHOSCOPE, 0, TOOL_CLASS, 1, 1, 0 }`, uncursed by definition at u_init.c:79. `pick_lock()`'s resume-an-interrupted-attempt branch (378-400) needs `gx.xlock.usedtime`, which `reset_pick()` is the port's only writer of and which is zero on a first application.

**A side effect worth pricing in.** `pick_lock()` is half of what `QUALITY.json`'s `an explicit autounlock setting is refused` says its fix belongs with, the other half being `autokey()`. Porting it does not close that entry — the entry waits on the parser for `flags.autounlock` — but it removes the `door unlocking tool` refusal at `js/hack.js:986-988` from the critical path, which is what currently caps `seed0007`'s `options` stretch at step 50.

**Why this goal and not the field.** Capped look-ahead on 6 August 2026 across fourteen candidates: this boundary 26 over two sessions with neither stretch cut, `#twoweapon` 25 of 35, `#pray` 21 of 21, pet combat evaluation 19 of 21, `takeoff` 18 of 18 over four, `fire` 17, monster trap activation 16, `options` 16 of 48, hero combat 15 over two, `wizgenesis` 11, riding movement 10 of 31, hero trap activation 8 of 61, engraving interaction 6 of 238, `#rub` 2 of 22. `options` led on the raw figure and on a first reading of its stretch, and it lost on the second: `seed0007` picks `lit_corridor` among its eight booleans, and `options.c:5362-5375` answers that option with `vision_recalc(2)`, `gv.vision_full_recalc = 1` and, because `color` is on and its address is `&iflags.wc_color` (optlist.h:236-238), `go.opt_need_redraw = TRUE`. `js/vision.js:746` skips at `control === 2` exactly the loop C runs there, and `reglyph_darkroom()` and `check_gold_symbol()` have no port at all — `js/do.js:855-864` and `:910-916` record both as deliberately unreachable. That caps `options` at step 36, where the picks are applied.

goals.detail:
### Clear the monsters area's deferral backlog

`npm run quality` at `0d3e6d3` names `monsters` at ten open non-`scope`
deferrals, and `.agents/selection.md`, "Deferred-area sweeps", requires
resolving one of an area's entries before the next boundary goal opens. Read
every entry in the area first; the reading costs more than the closing.

**Order.** The rule orders entries by how the port behaves at each one: an
entry where the port silently skips a message-writing C branch comes before one
where the port stops at a named refusal, because `AGENTS.md` forbids the first
and permits the second.

By that order the silent divergences lead:

- `gremlin-in-a-fountain` (production, small). Both `minLiquid` owners answer
  false for a fountain, so `mon.c:961 minliquid_core()`'s gremlin split at
  `:987` never draws its `rn2(3)`. Closable today by refusing.
- `artifactTouchable() crashes a segment instead of ending it` (production).
  `js/weapon.js:264-268` throws a bare `TypeError`, which costs the whole
  session prefix rather than ending the segment on its last matching screen.
  Same shape as `dosounds-refusal-escapes-as-hard-failure` in `world-effects`
  and `a live monster refusal escapes as a hard failure` in `startup`.
- `will-weld-ported-twice` (simplification, small). `js/wield.js:18-27` and
  `js/weapon.js:520-527` hold independent ports of `wield.c will_weld()` and
  `erodeable_wep()`. Opened by the `apply-tool-command` correctness pass, which
  applied the cross-reference comments and left the convergence here because
  `js/weapon.js` sat outside its reviewed range.
- The two planning-clone entries, `leaks by omission` and `must copy
  non-enumerable catalog aliases`. Both concern
  `preflightSimpleMonsterActions()`'s clone, which the next boundary goal will
  exercise hard whichever one is chosen.
- `one pickup assertion still does not discriminate` and `nine postmov findings
  are deferred`, both test-category.

**Expected survivors.** An entry closes only when the behavior its record names
as the closing condition is ported, so three are expected to survive on

`wield.c dotwoweapon()` (843-864) is the `#twoweapon` command. With

`.agents/selection.md` sets the reading order: an entry where the port skips a
message-writing C branch silently comes before one where the port stops on a

condition is ported, so an entry waiting on an unported command survives the
sweep and must be named in the closing report with the behavior it waits on.

goals.detail:
### Hero melee combat

`js/hack.js` raises `UnsupportedHeroMoveBoundaryError('hero combat or
displacement')` at three sites -- `:661-664` (counted repeated-command path),
`:1048-1051` (one-square walk, inside `requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap()`) and
`:1186-1188` (refused diagonal doorway). Three development sessions stop on it,
and porting it is worth 49 capped recorded steps, the largest capped figure in
the census at `6ec28b9`.

**What the C owns.** Spans confirmed by printing the first and last line of
each. Entry and target selection: `uhitm.c attack_checks()` 189-327 (139
lines), `find_roll_to_hit()` 365-427 (63), `do_attack()` 448-583 (136),
`known_hitum()` 587-646 (60), `hitum()` 758-815 (58), `hmon()` 819-834 (16, a
thin wrapper). Damage and messages: `hmon_hitmon()` 1754-1935 (182),
`hmon_hitmon_weapon()` 1070-1092 (23), `hmon_hitmon_weapon_melee()` 934-1067
(134), `hmon_hitmon_barehands()` 838-882 (45), `hmon_hitmon_do_hit()` 1387-1433
(47), `hmon_hitmon_dmg_recalc()` 1436-1507 (72), `hmon_hitmon_msg_hit()`
1637-1660 (24). The kill path all three witnesses reach: `mon.c monkilled()`
3377-3418 (42) and `xkilled()` 3477-3740 (264). Roughly 1,300 lines of C for
the paths the witnesses execute, which puts this goal over the 500-changed-line
threshold in `AGENTS.md` and requires a checklist.

**Already ported and reusable.** `js/uhitm.js:51 do_attack()` exists as an
84-line port covering only the safe-monster starting-pet branch, with
`is_safemon()` beside it; the hostile branch extends that function rather than
creating one. `js/hack.js:534 losehp()` is a working port -- it applies damage,
calls `showdamage()`, adjusts `uhpmax` and calls `maybe_wail()` -- and only its
`u.uhp < 1` and `Upolyd` branches raise `UnsupportedHitPointLossError`, so
hero-side damage taken during a fight already has an owner. `js/mhitm.js:77
mattackm()` ports the distant subset. Do not read any of these three as absent:
`grep -rn '\bdo_attack\b' js/` returns 13 and `doAttack` 0, `losehp` returns 8
and `loseHp` 0, `mattackm` returns 8 under both spellings.

**Genuinely new.** `grep -rnE
'\b(xkilled|xKilled|monkilled|monKilled|hitum|hmon|known_hitum|knownHitum|find_roll_to_hit|findRollToHit|attack_checks|attackChecks)\b'
js/` returns 4 hits, all of them comments in `js/steed.js:704`,
`js/trap_effects.js:245`, `js/trap_effects.js:250` and `js/const.js:2157` --
no definition and no call. Every function in the two "what the C owns" lists
above except `do_attack()` is unported. `xkilled()` is unavoidable: all three
witnesses record a kill on the refused step.

**Outside the boundary.** Force-fight (`F` prefix) and ranged attacks are not a
hero move into an occupied square and so fall outside the rule. Pet-versus-
monster melee is a different C file and a different system (`mhitm.c
mattackm()` 292-592, reached from `dogmove.c dog_move()`, refused at
`js/unported_monster_actions.js:727` as `attackMonster: () => unsupported('pet
combat')`) and is queued as its own goal; see "Pet melee" below for the figure.
Hero death stays refused at `js/hack.js` `losehp()`'s `u.uhp < 1` branch, since
`done(DIED)` and disclosure own the end of game; none of the three witnesses
dies on its capped stretch.

**How a reader tests the boundary.** Confirm that no `throw` site in `js/`
raises `UnsupportedHeroMoveBoundaryError` with the string `'hero combat or
displacement'`. Grepping for the string alone does not answer this:
`js/hack.js:1157` is a comment quoting it and will still match after the
boundary is met. Then replay the three witness sessions and confirm each
advances past its recorded stop step with screens and random-number calls
matching C.

**Why this and not the runner-up.** `movement while riding` caps at 31 over one
session against this goal's 49 over three, and its classifier block is flagged
ambiguous for an unexplained repeat marker and an untraced dismount message.
`engraving interaction` carries the largest raw figure in the census, 238, but
caps at 5.

**Pet melee, and why it is not in scope.** It has no census row of its own --
no session stops on it first, so its `unlocks` is 0; it surfaces only as a cap
inside other stretches. Lifting it does not restore those stretches, because
each is gated again immediately behind it: `seed0030`'s next recorded message
after "The kitten bites the newt.  The newt is killed!" is "Your kitten eats a
newt corpse.", and `seed0012`'s is "Your little dog eats a tripe ration." Both
need `dogmove.c dog_eat()`, which `chat-no-answer-arms-refused-as-one`
independently records as unported. So engraving moves 5 to about 6 and `#l` 1
to at most 19 -- roughly 13 to 19 steps in total, collectable only if engraving
and `#l` are also taken, and they rank 13th and 14th of 15. Decisively, none of
this goal's own three sessions is capped by pet melee, so taking it in scope
buys 0 of the 49 while adding about 300 lines of C in a second file and a
second game system to a goal already needing a checklist. Queued after rather
than with, because both paths need `mon.c xkilled()` and `monkilled()`, which
hero combat must port for its own three "You kill the ...!" lines; a pet-melee
goal that follows inherits a working kill path instead of competing for it.

**On the `js/hack.js` line numbers above.** They are correct at
`910ca6f`. They drifted 6 to 15 lines between the scan at `6ec28b9` and this
goal opening, because `daae919` and `1feb4cf` landed in between, and the
record as first written sent a reader into `carriesUnlockingTool()`. Print the
line before trusting any of them.


### The remaining slices, and what they carry

Slices 1 and 2 closed at `fabbb65` and `b266364`. Three remain, and the
goal's whole 49 steps sit behind the last two.

**Slice 3, the hit arm.** `uhitm.c hmon()` 819-834 and `hmon_hitmon()`
1754-1935 with 11 live helpers, not the 7 first recorded. `_do_hit` 1387-1433,
`_pet` 1588-1601, `_splitmon` 1604-1634 and `_msg_hit` 1637-1660 are called
unconditionally at 1795, 1866, 1868 and 1870; `_dmg_recalc` 1436-1507,
`_stagger` 1570-1585, `_barehands` 838-882, `_weapon` 1070-1092 and
`_weapon_melee` 934-1067 are guarded and live. `_pet` and `_splitmon` need only
be proven no-ops for a hostile non-pudding but must exist. `_stagger` fires for
any bare-handed hit with `dmg > 1` and draws `rnd(100)`, which seed0200's Monk
pays. `_msg_hit` prints nothing on a killing blow -- its guard at 1642-1645
requires `!destroyed` -- so a non-fatal hit is the only case that exercises it,
and merging slice 3 into slice 4 would ship it with no end-to-end evidence.
Worth 0 of the 49. Consumes `artifact_light()` at `_weapon_melee`:1038 and must
converge the five existing copies rather than adding a sixth, per
`artifact-light-ported-five-times`.

**Slice 4, the kill.** `mon.c killed()` 3469-3473 and `xkilled()` 3477-3740,
with `mondead()` 3081-3177, `m_detach()` 2734-2803, `mon_leaving_level()`
2696-2730, `lifesaved_monster()` 2839-2884, `corpse_chance()` 3181-3249,
`make_corpse()` 564-941, `exper.c experience()` 85-166 and `attrib.c adjalign()`
1298-1316. Worth 39 of the 49: it moves seed0200 and seed0006. About 700 lines
of C of which about 400 are live.

`xkilled()` cannot be split by position. The witnesses' route is one straight
line inside a single keystroke and it draws in the middle -- `rn2(6)` for the
treasure drop at 3587 and `corpse_chance()`'s `rn2(tmp)` at 3248 both sit
between the kill message and `experience()` -- so a port stopping short desyncs
on the next call and moves none of the three. It lands whole, at about 131 live
lines of its 264; roughly 133 are arms no witness reaches and become named
refusals.

**Slice 5, the second attack.** `uhitm.c hitum()` 791-812 and `double_punch()`
736-754, with the `hmd.twohits` threading at 1765. Worth 10 of the 49: it moves
seed0107, whose recorded moves open with `#twoweapon` and whose step 15 reads
"You begin two-weapon combat.", so `u.twoweap` is true from step 15 and step 40
emits two outcomes from one keystroke. Without this arm seed0107 does not move
and its 10 steps are stranded. It is a damage-math variant rather than a loop
iteration: `u.twoweap` at 955 disables Rogue backstab and the `dieroll == 2`
shatter arm, `_dmg_recalc` takes the 3/4 strength branch at 1465 rather than the
bimanual 3/2, `weapon_dam_bonus()` returns -3 because `P_TWO_WEAPON_COMBAT`
starts Unskilled, `use_skill()` trains two-weapon rather than the short sword,
and `maybe_knockback` is suppressed.

### Traps the remaining slices must not walk into

`maybe_knockback` is computed at `uhitm.c`:1829-1831 and discarded at 1923
whenever the monster dies, so a port that evaluates `mhitm_knockback()` eagerly
desyncs the random-number stream on every kill.

Silver damage is added at two independent sites and must not be double-counted:
`rnd(20)` inside `dmgval` at `weapon.c`:332 for weapons, and `rnd(20)` inside
`special_dmgval` at `weapon.c`:403, 412 and 422 for bare hands, added at
`uhitm.c`:861.

The retaliation wall bites slice 3 hardest. `js/unported_monster_actions.js`
refuses a monster attack on the hero the moment an adjacent monster acts. A kill
removes the monster, which is why the three witnesses get through; a hit that
does not kill leaves it alive and adjacent. Slice 2 escaped by picking targets
slow enough that `js/mon.js`:312 returns before `dochug()`, and slice 3 needs
the same, on the narrower window of a hit that fails to kill.

`corpse_chance()` computes `tmp = 2 + ((geno & G_FREQ) < 2) + verysmall(mdat)`,
giving sewer rat 4, lichen 2 and goblin 2 -- the goblin's frequency is 2, which
fails `< 2`, reaching the lichen's divisor by a different route. The witnesses
split the branch: seed0006's rat leaves bare floor, the lichen and goblin each
leave a corpse.

`js/makemon_create.js` holds a merged port of `mon_leaving_level()` plus
`m_detach()` plus `mongone()` for the `due_to_death` FALSE case, and it discards
inventory. The kill path needs `m_detach(mtmp, mptr, TRUE)`, which calls
`relobj()` to drop it. Slice 4 must either extract a shared `m_detach()` into
`js/mon.js` and rewire `mongone()`, or knowingly split `mon.c` across two files.

### Two state-ownership questions, settled before slice 3 starts

`struct _hitmon_data` (`include/you.h`:511-552, 27 fields) becomes a plain
JavaScript object created in `hmon_hitmon()` and threaded through the helpers by
reference. It is per-call scratch: C allocates it on the stack at 1760 and it
dies when the function returns, so a durable home would create a second place
for values that already live on `mon`, `uwep` and `u`. Initialize all 27 fields
explicitly in definition order matching 1763-1793, because the `you.h`:518-521
comment records that the ordering of `first_weapon_hit()` against the hit-point
decrement is exactly what the struct exists to preserve.

`gt.twohits` is genuine turn-scoped state with one owner in `js/uhitm.js`,
written only by `hitum()`. C writes it at 776 and 800, clears it at 813, 5449
and 5857, and increments it at 5524 for polymorphed multi-claw attacks, which is
why `hmon_hitmon_barehands` carries a `default:` arm for values of 3 or more. It
never survives a turn and never reaches storage, so it belongs on neither
`game` nor `input.storage`. `hmon_hitmon()` must copy it into `hmd.twohits` at
1765 with the ranged zeroing rather than reading the global downstream; that
copy is why ranged attacks do not take the two-weapon damage branches.

### One stale refusal to clear before the goal closes

`js/hack.js` still raises `'hero combat or displacement'` inside
`requireSimpleHeroDestination()`, which `domove()` reaches only when the
destination holds no monster. It is dead from `hack.c` but live from
`js/teleport.js`, where a teleport destination can hold a monster. The goal's
own completion test greps for that string, so the site needs renaming or
removing before the boundary reads as met.

goals.detail:
### The hero checks skills with `#enhance`

`seed0107-samurai-twoweapon-enhance` stops at step 50 of 98 on the Return that
completes `#enhance`. `js/extcmdlist_data.js:64` already binds the command to
its C name, so the seam exists and only the body is absent.

**What the C owns.** Spans confirmed by printing the first and last line of
each. `weapon.c enhance_weapon_skill()` 1329-1407 (79 lines),
`add_skills_to_menu()` 1224-1302 (79), `could_advance()` 1171-1182 (12),
`peaked_skill()` 1184-1195 (12), and the `skill_ranges[]` table 1215-1222 (8).
About 190 lines of new C. `skill_advance()` 1197-1213 and `dump_skills()` from
1304 stay outside.

**Already ported, reuse rather than re-port.** `can_advance()` is
`js/weapon.js:1280`, `skill_level_name()` is `:1115`, `slots_required()` is
`:1268`; `practice_needed_to_advance()` and `P_NAME` are in the same file.
`grep -rlw` finds `enhance_weapon_skill` only in `js/extcmdlist_data.js`, and
`add_skills_to_menu`, `could_advance` and `peaked_skill` in no file at all,
under either spelling. Only `P_RESTRICTED` and `skill_ranges[]` are missing
data.

**The menu renderer exists.** `js/tty_menu.js selectTtyMenu()` already draws
headings, paginates, and prints the `(N of M)` footer, and `js/cmd.js:1085`
already maps `item.heading` onto `menuTitleStyle()` for the inventory and spell
menus. The recorded screen's reverse-video headings and `(1 of 2)` footer are
what it renders today.

**Why the whole advancement half is out of reach here, and how a reader checks
it.** The recorded menu carries no `*` or `#` legend, which fixes
`eventually_advance == 0` and `maxxed_cnt == 0` at :1362. Its title reads
`Current skills:` rather than `Pick a skill to advance:`, which fixes
`to_advance == 0` at :1383. Those three zeros make `selectable` false at
:1380-1381, and independently every skill line starts at the same column with no
selector, which is `add_skills_to_menu()`'s `!selectable` arm at :1266-1267. So
`select_menu()` runs `PICK_NONE` and `skill_advance()` cannot execute. A reader
tests the boundary by confirming those three counters are zero on the witness
and that no production path calls `skill_advance()`.

**The wizard half is unreachable for a separate reason** and stays refused: the
`y_n` prompt at :1340-1341, `can_advance()`'s `wizard && speedy` shortcut at
:1163-1164, the wizard column format at :1277-1287, and the
`(%d slot%s available)` title suffix at :1385-1387. The witness rc sets no
`playmode`.

**Two residual risks, both audited clear.**
`full-screen-menu-dismissal-repaints-status` covers the ESC at step 51, but its
own record states the exposure needs a second window inside one command with no
intervening message, and step 52 opens a fresh command.
`twoweapon-unreachable-refusal-arms` cannot fire, because no role starts with an
artifact and `u_init.c:1223` clears cursed on every starting object.

**Why this and not the runner-up.** The options menu
(`options.c doset_simple_menu()` 8534-8702, 169 lines) caps at 23-24 on
`seed0006`. `#enhance` is roughly half again as large a stretch from a third of
the C, and every step behind it is already-ported `#twoweapon` and `#chat`
rather than new behavior. The options menu also opens a second window
immediately -- the `Autopickup what?` class submenu at steps 50-56 -- which
would drag `optfn_pickup_types` and the menu-dismissal repaint defect into the
same goal.

**A note on the figure.** The forecast is 34 against a raw 35, discounting step
51, the one step whose screen could not be verified against a live replay. The
`hero-combat` goal that closed before this one forecast 49 and delivered 25
because a flagged low-confidence block was discounted in the argument and left
at full value in the number; this record discounts it in the number.

`js/hack.js:897` today refuses a hero move onto **any** trap square regardless of
type. Retiring that in favour of `dotrap()`'s dispatcher is what this goal buys
beyond its 24 steps: every later hero trap type arrives behind a switch that
already exists.

`trap.c dotrap()` 2995-3060 (66 lines), `trapeffect_bear_trap()` 1478-1560 (83,

3912-3933, `conjoined_pits()` 6551-6577, `adj_nonconjoined_pit()` 6603-6614;

plus the `wriggle_free:` label at 1671) and `spoteffects()`'s `pick && !pit`
ordering at 3373-3398; `mon.c monkilled()` 3376-3418; `do.c
set_wounded_legs()` 2425-2446. About 360 lines actually in the arms.

trap')`), and `trapeffect_pit()` passes `d_override = rnd(6)`, which forces

### The objects area's ten non-scope deferrals

`npm run quality -- deferrals` names `objects` at ten, counting every category
except `scope`. The area holds twelve entries; the two `scope` ones name
unported territory a boundary goal attacks and are not swept.

The ten, unordered:

- Escape at the wish prompt still grants a random wish (production, slice)
- a wish that matches nothing is not retried (production, slice)
- wishymatch() folds case where C's strsubst() does not (production, slice)
- five wish-parser test gaps the pass confirmed (tests, slice)
- a wished-for container stops the segment at mkbox_cnts() (production, slice)
- pickup-merged-gold-weight (production, slice)
- object-predicates-ported-under-mixed-spellings (simplification, small)
- doname-twoweap-guard-too-broad (production, small)
- artifact-light-ported-five-times (production, small)
- armoroff() refuses every piece with a non-zero oc_delay (production, slice)

`.agents/selection.md` sets the reading order: an entry where the port skips a
message-writing C branch silently comes before one where it stops on a named
refusal, because `AGENTS.md` forbids the first and permits the second. On that
test the three wish-parser production entries read first -- `wishymatch()`
folding case and the un-retried no-match are both silent divergences -- and the
entries whose records say "refuses" or "stops" read last.

Three are expected to close, taking the area from ten to seven:
`artifact-light-ported-five-times`, whose five copies the hero-combat slice was
told to converge and did not; `object-predicates-ported-under-mixed-spellings`;
and `doname-twoweap-guard-too-broad`. The first of those is the eighth duplicate
port of the twelve found here in eight days, and its bodies disagree -- C guards
`obj &&` in its first clause and `js/timeout.js` does not, so that copy throws a
TypeError where C returns FALSE.

An entry closes only when the behavior its record names as the closing condition
is ported, so an entry waiting on an unported command survives the sweep and
must be named in the closing report with the behavior it waits on. Two are
already expected to survive on that test: `armoroff()` waits on `nomul()`, which
the open "nomul() has two owners and they disagree" entry blocks, and the five
wish-parser entries wait on wish-parser work no goal has scheduled.

**Correction, recorded at close.** The paragraph above says the
`hero-combat` slice "was told to converge them and did not". That is wrong.
`4d2a9cb`, the melee-hit slice, converged all five copies into
`js/artifacts.js:833`: `grep -rn "function artifact_light" js/ scripts/`
returns one line and `grep -rn artifactLight` returns 0. The claim was the
orchestrator’s, made from the deferral record rather than from the tree, and
it also sits in this goal’s opening commit `8f14eca`, which cannot be amended.
Two of the ten records were wrong the same way — already fixed and never
closed — and `armoroff()`’s named blocker was stale, since `daae919` gave
`nomul()` one port. A deferral record ages against a tree that keeps moving,
and reading it as current is the mistake this sweep exists to catch.

goals.detail:
### Refusals that discard what the port already earned

A refusal that escapes `runSegment()` does not cost the branch it stops; it
costs **every matching screen before it**. That is measured twice:
`seed0015` scored 0 of 44 where it already had 28, and five consecutive goal
selections ran under a loader shim because two throws killed the census.

**Slice 1, verified by hand.** `UnsupportedSearchError` is listed in
`js/cmd.js:974`'s `failClosedCommandRefusals()` and absent from
`js/allmain.js`'s `elapsedTurnPlanningRefusals()`, while `js/allmain.js:679`
calls `automatic_search({ state, random })` outside any converting `try`. A
Ranger has intrinsic searching from experience level 1, so this fires every
turn for that role. Same defect as `dosounds`, one seam up, with a *named*
class — which is why grepping for `throw new Error(` would not have found it.

**Slice 2, five named and unverified.** `js/dungeon.js:1249 surface()`, reached
by `:` and by pickup, where `js/hack.js:895` converts only the movement route;
`js/detect.js:262`, per-turn, in a file that already has a named class it does
not use; `js/mktrap.js:511`'s web spider; and four des-file interpreter arms at
`js/mklev.js:667`, `:808`, `:831`, `:940`. **Each must be verified before it is
converted** — this repository has had nineteen "X is unreachable" claims come
out wrong in eight days, and the survey that produced this list was delegated,
not checked.

An escape shown genuinely unreachable needs a derivation recorded beside it, not
a conversion. Converting an unreachable path adds a refusal class nothing can
raise, which is the mirror of the problem.

**Why this is not ranked.** `.agents/selection.md` ranks boundary ports on
capped development look-ahead, and this goal forecasts no steps. It is scheduled
on the user's instruction against that rule, on the two measured costs above.
The third cost I offered — twelve holdout screens — turned out not to belong to
this class at all: an authorized attribution run at `74c622c` showed the
movement came from `do.c dodrop()`. That correction is at `9d26680`, and this
goal carries no holdout expectation.

**What the fix is not.** `js/` holds 316 plain `throw new Error(` sites. Most
are internal assertions on paths no session reaches, and converting them
wholesale would be speculative work of exactly the kind `AGENTS.md` defers. The
boundary is *reachable* escapes, and reachability is the thing to establish
first.

THE SCOPE DECISION, AND THE 17-VERSUS-137 SPLIT. Scoped to
trapeffect_bear_trap()'s monster arm alone, this goal is worth 17 steps:
seed0004 would run from step 34 to step 50 and stop at step 51, where
js/timeout.js:270-282 ends the segment on the turn the wounded-legs count
reaches zero. Scoped to the bear trap end to end -- the monster arm, the turns
the trapped monster spends before pulling free, and the wounded-legs recovery
that ends the hero's own bear-trap wound -- it is worth 137. The goal opened
here is the wider one, and 137 is the figure it is calibrated against at close.

The reason for the wider scope is that heal_legs() is not adjacent to this
behavior; it is the other end of it. The wound is written at trap.c:1520,
inside trapeffect_bear_trap()'s own hero arm, by
set_wounded_legs(rn2(2) ? RIGHT_SIDE : LEFT_SIDE, rn1(10, 10)), and heal_legs()
is the only path in the game that clears it. js/do.js:1446-1450 already says so
in the port: "timeout.c nh_timeout() counts the intrinsic down and calls
heal_legs() at zero. heal_legs() is not ported, so js/timeout.js stops the
segment on the turn the count would reach zero." A goal that catches a monster
in a bear trap and then stops the segment 6 turns later because the hero's own
bear-trap wound expires would file itself complete with a documented hole in
the middle of its own behavior. .agents/selection.md covers exactly this: "A
second behavior recurring across many sessions' stretches is scope the goal
should include, counted in the forecast from the start." An independent
classifier run over this stretch capped it at 51 and argued heal_legs() was
orthogonal; it was costing the narrower goal because the brief it was given
named only the three monster-side owners. That was a defect in the brief, and
this paragraph exists so the next reader does not re-derive the argument.

WHAT IS PORTED TODAY, WHAT IS NOT, AND WHERE THE PORT REFUSES.

- Ported: trapeffect_bear_trap()'s HERO arm, at js/trap_effects.js:485-547,

  branches -- the mounted arm at C 1507-1511 and the iron-shoes line at C

  inside the arm, and stay out of scope.
- Ported: every helper the monster arm reads. wearing_iron_shoes() at

  at :129-130, m_in_air() at js/monmove.js:653, Monnam() as
  capitalizedMonsterName() at js/do_name.js:238, and set_msg_xy() as
  messageAt() at js/startup_a11y.js:294. The port's own comment at

- Ported: every helper heal_legs() reads. body_part() at js/polyself.js:187,
  vtense() at js/objnam.js:529, makeplural() at js/fruit.js:293,
  encumber_msg() at js/pickup.js:80. makeplural() is not on this path:

  better.", matching the recording.
- Not ported, four refusal sites, all of which this goal lifts.
  js/trap_effects.js:491 `if (!is_you) unsupported('a monster caught in a bear
  trap')`; js/trap_effects.js:811 `if (monster.mtrapped) unsupported('a monster
  escaping a trap')` inside the ported mintrap(); js/unported_monster_actions.js

  UnsupportedHeroTimeoutBoundaryError('heal_legs() for an expiring wounded-legs

gnew dirty-bbox discipline that flush_screen() needs, so the 7 screens do not
require converting _buildScreenOutput(). If the sweep finds them inseparable,
that entry survives and the forecast drops to 0. Whoever takes the slice should

mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: doorganize() for the extended command 'adjust' is not ported

result.summary: invent.c owns the #adjust boundary: doorganize() selects an inventory source object with getobj("adjust", ...), then doorganize_core() asks for a destination letter and performs collect, move, merge, swap, or split bookkeeping. At the refreshed stop, the C recording has just painted What do you want to adjust? [a-km or ?*] after #adjust; JavaScript has the adjust and altadjust rows plus item-action queue wiring, but js/cmd.js doextcmd() lacks doorganize and adjust_split cases and falls into its generic refusal before invent.js getobj() runs. Port the complete invent.c adjust family and wire both handlers, preserving inventory-chain ordering, object names, messages, redraw, cancellation, malformed-gold handling, and split/count paths.

source.branch: doorganize() returns ECMD_OK with a no-adjustable message only for an empty inventory or a sole gold stack already in '$'; otherwise !fixinv first reassigns letters, check_invent_gold("adjust") selects a filter that excludes ordinary gold or admits malformed gold, and getobj("adjust", filter, GETOBJ_PROMPT | GETOBJ_ALLOWCNT) chooses the source. doorganize_core() then accepts cancel, same-letter collection, a different destination for move/merge/swap, or a counted split; adjust_split() is the internal item-action path for non-gold stacks of at least two and validates a split count before calling splitobj(). The assigned recording has the normal fixed-letter path, a named long sword in slot a, and destination z, with no RNG at the boundary.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1673-1674 binds the M-a/adjust extended-command row to doorganize(); js/extcmdlist_data.js:45 already preserves that row, while js/cmd.js:4885-5150 has no doorganize case and reaches its default refusal.

nethack-c/upstream/src/iactions.c:191-197 queues doorganize or adjust_split followed by the selected inventory letter; js/iactions.js:295-302 mirrors both queues, so the same production handlers must serve item-actions.
nethack-c/upstream/src/invent.c:4981-5003 is the user entrypoint and :5008-5064 is the internal split entrypoint; both converge on :5068-5279 doorganize_core().
dependencies: invent.c:4889-4913 check_invent_gold(), :739-765 reorder_invent(), and reassign() provide gold validation, inventory ordering, and !fixinv relabeling; js/invent.js already has check_invent_gold(), reassign(), and the equivalent private reorderInventory().

doorganize_core() uses invent.c mergable()/merged(), extract_nobj(), inv_cnt(), assigninvlet(), clear_splitobjs(), prinv(), and update_inventory(); the existing JS ports are js/invent.js, js/obj.js, and js/hack.js, but their state and message ordering must be preserved while wiring the new owner.

The destination ?/* branch calls invent.c:3467-3518 display_used_invlets(), which paints a selectable Inventory letters used menu and returns a letter or cancel; no display_used_invlets owner exists in js/invent.js, so this return-valued dependency is part of the source-general scope.

The GETOBJ_ALLOWCNT source branch at invent.c:1937-1947 and adjust_split() at :5022-5040 consume get_count(); js/invent.js:832-843 currently raises UnsupportedObjectPromptError for get_count() and splitobj(), so counted adjust and the internal stack-split path need explicit completion or a recorded dependency handoff.

C defers prinv() and update_inventory() until the inventory chain has been restored (:5262-5279); js/invent.js:3267-3283 and :1727-1740 provide those output/refresh seams, while object names and merge side effects flow through the existing object and inventory modules.

evidence: .cache/scan-cache.json at SHA 242d3d77cbff92156ce9bdf95eb0404a12ae7fa7 reports the assigned row at screensEmitted 733, recordedSteps 1814, and the exact doorganize refusal; 1814 - 733 = remainingScreensUpperBound 1081.

sessions/holdout/seed4500-knight-coverage.session.json segment 0 steps 726-733 type #adjust and adjust; step 733 has key newline, zero RNG, and the C prompt What do you want to adjust? [a-km or ?*]. Steps 734-735 answer source a and destination z, with the C Moving: z - a ... Sword of Justice result, proving the actionable path continues through doorganize_core().

nethack-c/upstream/src/invent.c:4915-5279 defines adjust_ok(), adjust_gold_ok(), doorganize(), adjust_split(), and doorganize_core(); the core performs exact collection/merge/swap/split ordering and restores the inventory before messages and update_inventory().

nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1673-1674 and :2062 plus js/extcmdlist_data.js:45 and :209 establish the public adjust and internal altadjust bindings; js/iactions.js:295-302 establishes the live item-action callers, while js/cmd.js doextcmd() lacks both switch cases and emits the observed default refusal.

The actionable scope is a source-general invent.c file-port family with command dispatch wiring and the return-valued display_used_invlets/count dependencies; do not special-case seed 4500, the Knight role, the named sword, the chosen letters, or step 733.

functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/monmove.c:1454-1705 in full and compared every branch, state write, message/redraw order, and return-value test with js/monmove.js. The JavaScript implementation keeps the source-order seenFlags, canTunnel, canUnlock, canOpen signature at every production m_move() call; brackets mintrap() and its killed/moved/off-map returns with the source redraw; refreshes species after mintrap; preserves the magic-key D_TRAPPED disarm; uses source whole-mask door conditions and mb_trapped() results; calls existing detect.c, vision.c, trap.c, dig.c, mon.c, and artifact.c owners; sets hero ux0/uy0 before u_on_newpos(); keeps C ELSE redraw semantics for swallowing; calls meatmetal/meatobj/meatcorpse and checks their exact source statuses; propagates mpickstuff; repaints minvis and records the discarded worm.c see_wsegs gap; runs maybe_spin_web and concealment in order; and calls after_shk_move(). The web helper uses the existing naming/display owners and source soko_allow_web clear_path test. The monster artifact gate is synchronous and shares touch_artifact() restrictions, while m_consume_obj() calls healmon() before delobj() as C does. Gaps are limited to discarded-result or planning-display callees explicitly named in the entryPointReview: worm.c see_wsegs, display.c swallowed clone redraw without a callback, and shk.c add_damage. No new Unsupported refusal stands in for a selected postmov branch. Integration also wires the already-ported ttyNorep owner for ordinary iron-bars passage, with source locomotion/makeplural wording and planning suppression; the adjacent bars-eating message uses the C pline_mon location wrapper.

functions.name: num_extinct
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/insight.c:2969-2981 in full. The source loops from LOW_PM through NUMMONS, skips UniqCritterIndx entries, and increments only when (svm.mvitals[i].mvflags & G_GONE) == G_EXTINCT. The JavaScript reads the caller's state-owned svm.mvitals and mons in the same order, has no random draw, output, or mutation, and preserves the PM_HIGH_CLERIC UniqCritterIndx exception through the existing isUniqueMonster owner.

callers.source: insight.c:list_genocided calls num_extinct only when final disclosure, wizard, or explore mode exposes extinctions.

functions.name: num_gone
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/insight.c:2984-3003 in full. The source clears its compact index array, walks LOW_PM through NUMMONS, skips UniqCritterIndx entries, and appends each index whose mvflags intersect the uchar mask. The JavaScript returns the compact indexes in that same order from state-owned mvitals, with no random draw, output, or state mutation; clearing the temporary C array has no observable JavaScript counterpart.

callers.source: insight.c:list_genocided calls num_gone with G_GENOD and conditionally G_EXTINCT before filtering the disclosure list.

functions.name: list_genocided
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/insight.c:3006-3131 in full. The port preserves dumping and genoing query conversion, the gameover/wizard/discover extinction gate, count and mask evaluation order, the single-versus-multiple yn response strings, q stopprint handling, y/a admission, shared set_vanq_order selection, count-mode temporary alpha-mix substitution and restoration, class headers, plural names and exact extinct marker, blank lines, summaries, text-window display, and the ordinary no-entry pline. Existing set_vanq_order, vanqsort_cmp, ttyPline, and displayTtyMenuTextWindow owners are called directly; no random call or invented side effect substitutes a missing callee. The DUMPLOG game-over putstr arm is explicitly compile-time excluded from this recorder build. The final-disclosure caller supplies the existing yn_function owner, while the command caller uses the non-asking source path. Correction verification: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/insight.c:3006-3131 in full. Its class_header branch calls putstr with ask ? ATR_NONE : iflags.menu_headings.attr before upstart(buf). The correction preserves that exact condition and passes the resulting attr on the heading line while leaving titles, blank lines, species rows, extinct suffixes, and totals unstyled. The existing tty text-window owner already consumes line.attr, so no alternate display state or invented output path was added.

functions.name: dogenocided

The wrapper selects 'a' only when iflags.menu_requested is set, otherwise 'y', calls list_genocided with ask FALSE, and returns ECMD_OK without clearing menu_requested. The JavaScript keeps that exact flag read, delegates the complete list family, and returns ECMD_OK; the resulting disclosure output is therefore owned by list_genocided rather than reconstructed here.

source.branch: Whole top-level dat/Wiz-filb.lua program (lines 6-58): six ordinary rooms with source-ordered up/down stairs, objects, traps, hostile class-X/class-i monsters, vampire bats, and a final random-corridors directive. On Quest Home 4, C mklev.c makelevel() selects the "filb" suffix because u.uz.dlevel is at or below the Wizard locate level, then unconditionally calls makemaz("Wiz-filb"); load_special() executes this complete Lua chunk after nhlib.lua shuffles its private alignment table. The JavaScript branch only calls makemaz when SPECIAL_LEVEL_LOADERS["Wiz-filb"] exists, so the missing loader sends this level into ordinary generation and changes RNG order before any room generation.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/mklev.c:1275-1285 makelevel() handles In_quest levels, forms <role-filecode>-filb for this dlevel, and unconditionally calls makemaz(fillname).

nethack-c/upstream/src/mkmaze.c:1184-1195 makemaz() appends the level extension and calls sp_lev.c load_special() for the selected prototype; nethack-c/upstream/src/sp_lev.c owns the Lua descriptor execution and post-processing.

js/mklev.js:692-707 makelevel() computes Wiz-filb and only calls makemaz() if the registry contains a loader; with no Wiz-filb entry it falls through to the medusa check and regular generation at lines 709-727.

js/mklev.js:1762-1783 load_special() and lines 1786-1815 makemaz() are the production JavaScript special-level dispatcher, while js/quest_levels.js:1829-1852 supplies QUEST_LEVEL_LOADERS and currently registers Wiz-fila without Wiz-filb.
dependencies: nethack-c/upstream/dat/Wiz-filb.lua:6-58 is the complete source program: six ordinary-room descriptors, an up stair in the first room, a down stair in the fourth, object/trap/monster calls, and des.random_corridors().
nethack-c/upstream/dat/nhlib.lua:17-25 implements shuffle(); loading a special level consumes rn2(3) then rn2(2) for the three-entry alignment table before Wiz-filb.lua executes.
nethack-c/upstream/src/mklev.c:1275-1285 is the Quest filler selection precondition; at dnum 3, dlevel 4, with Wiz-loca at dlevel 3, the selected prototype is Wiz-filb.
nethack-c/upstream/src/mkmaze.c:1184-1195 and sp_lev.c load_special() define the C loader path that the JavaScript registry and special-level API must reproduce.

js/quest_levels.js:1788-1852 has the existing Wiz-fila implementation and registry convention, but no Wiz-filb program or registry entry; this is why the current makelevel() fallback reaches ordinary generation.

Ported the guard order for guards, non-revival shopkeepers, high and aligned clerics, angels, long-worm tails, and unique corpses or statues. The returned mtype is kept alongside changed, and the unique arm preserves C's !from_obj || !has_omonst() test. The read.c creation caller consumes both the replacement and force-choice result; trap.c animate_statue() and zap.c stone_to_flesh_obj() retain their existing callers.
