callers.source: read.c:3259-3269; creation assigns the replacement species before the wizard force prompt and consumes the returned mtype.
trap.c:746-754; statue revival uses cant_revive() before selecting saved traits or a fresh replacement.
zap.c:982-994; figurine conversion consumes the possible species substitution before makemon().

functions.name: create_particular_parse
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:3137-3251 in full. Preserved the initial quantity from gm.multi, digit-by-digit count consumption, QUAN_LIMIT and monster_census(FALSE) fallback, the source ordered case-insensitive gear/state/gender searches with in-place blanking, mungspaces(), disposition prefixes, wizard-only * and random handling, name_to_mon() gender output, explicit gender conflict, and the name_to_monclass() concrete, invisible, worm-tail, class, and failure arms. The returned request is local data; its inputs include the hero role, command count, wizard flag, source census and initialized monster catalog. No random draw, message, or game-state mutation occurs. Supporting minion.c monster_census40–57 is pure: it traverses the live monster list, excludes dead monsters and guards with mx zero, and applies canonical canspotmon only for a spotted census. The source-pinned test covers these filters, including the default sensing predicate.

callers.source: read.c:3382-3388; each getlin() answer is munged and passed to create_particular_parse() before creation or the retry diagnostics.

functions.name: create_particular_creation
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:3252-3371 in full. Preserved the non-random firstchoice and cant_revive replacement before the y_n force prompt, then source ordered mkclass()/rndmonst() selection, explicit gender conflict and MM_NOEXCLAM/MM_MINVIS flags, makemon() return and retry behavior, tamedog/set_malign disposition arms, saddle creation after can_saddle/which_armor, hidden tests for M1_HIDE, M1_CONCEAL plus OBJ_AT, and eel plus is_pool, sleeping state, flash_mon() and final newcham() order. The makemon caller is awaited through its runtime continuation; its marker admits both ordinary MM_NOEXCLAM requests and the C gender-conflict arm that has only one gender bit, with optional MM_MINVIS. mon_set_minvis() remains after placement and peace_minded() as in makemon.c:1299-1301. The caller now awaits canonical mon.c flash_mon(), which completes the whole display.c flash_glyph_at() animation before creation continues. Independent hidden-trapper and invisible-newt recordings match each source animation frame, final screen, cursor and RNG sequence; the underlying temporary vision, ordinary mon_to_glyph and hero-memory background behavior is recorded with the display.c source goal.

callers.source: read.c:3405; a successful parse reaches create_particular_creation() and returns its Boolean result.

functions.name: create_particular
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:3372-3411 in full. Preserved the five-attempt countdown, Escape return, parse retry diagnostics and first retry prompt extension, then the final enough-tries message or awaited creation return. The source result is carried through both production callers; no fire-and-forget creation remains. The command seam no longer lists an obsolete monster-request refusal class because unknown text follows this source retry loop. Integration uses the canonical thats_enough_tries constant from decl.c common strings. A production-caller unit test verifies that four invalid answers retain the expanded prompt and a fifth ends the retry loop, with normal message acknowledgements between answers; it pins the source exclamation mark.

callers.source: wizcmds.c:203-210; wizard #wizgenesis clears debug_mongen, awaits create_particular(), restores the flag, and returns ECMD_OK.
makemon.c:1569-1577; the wizard create-monster scroll/wand/spell path awaits create_particular() and uses its Boolean to continue or stop prompting.

Active class/random, saddle, tame, explicit gender-conflict, force-revival, create_critters scroll/spell, and bones.c, trap.c and zap.c cant_revive families retain empty recording arrays until their own production routes are exercised. functions.name: do_screen_description
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/pager.c:1247-1630 in full, together with add_cmap_descr():1133-1244 and append_str():82-104. The port preserves restricted-vision and swallow ordering, monster/object/misc/cmap/warning/venom passes, rotated water/lava aliases, trap and drawbridge suppression, optional overrides with source re-entry, many-things refinement, and final lookat refinement. It uses the C boulder fallback and Is_rogue_level selection, independent NOTHING/UNEXPLORED glyph checks, DEF_INVISIBLE semantics, source warning co-location text, temporary EHalluc_resistance and terrain restoration, stored-glyph pet override handling without a live-monster guard, and BUFSZ-bounded case-insensitive append_str behavior. The typed one-byte caller enters the same renderer and emits the C no-match message. Existing discarded or unported caller families remain explicitly open rather than represented by invented behavior. Canonical display.c map_glyphinfo now resolves unexplored, warning and stored monster glyph families without reading rendered cell sidecars or rerolling glyph selection. Lookup uses selected coordinates, while the encoded prefix follows windows.c decode_mixed and utf8map.c mixed_to_utf8 at (0,0). Supporting glyph resolution preserves pet override before hero handling, the independent NOOVERRIDE pet reset, nonzero hero-space overrides, the literal showsyms[pet_override] test, and Rogue monster/warning colors with the stored-map clamp before hero showrace adjustment. Literal source-pinned assertions cover ant-class fallback at ordinary and hero coordinates and zero-byte pet overrides with a customized stone symbol.

callers.source: pager.c do_look() dispatches ordinary map farlook, quick look, and typed one-character symbol lookup to do_screen_description(); the JavaScript command routes these paths through the complete renderer.
getpos.c auto_describe() requests a description for the selected displayed map cell; the JavaScript caller uses the canonical pager path.
cmd.c doclicklook() dispatches the clicked look path to the shared description behavior; JavaScript command dispatch reaches the canonical pager renderer for displayed cells.
cmd.c dolookaround() scans source-interesting stored glyphs and calls do_screen_description; JavaScript uses the same stored-glyph filter and canonical renderer.
display.c show_glyph() requests the first description after installing a glyph; startup accessibility queues this production notice through do_screen_description().
cmd.c dolookaround() describes visible interesting cells; the accessibility lookaround caller validates a displayed glyph and invokes the shared do_screen_description() path.

evidence.entryPointReview: This is the complete pager.c do_screen_description source unit, including its add_cmap_descr and append_str contracts. Production callers reviewed are pager.c do_look (ordinary, quick, and typed symbol paths), getpos.c auto_describe, cmd.c doclicklook and dolookaround, and display.c show_glyph through the startup accessibility caller. Existing sink/fountain farlook recordings exercise displayed cmap collection; independently selected typed comma recordings exercise the one-byte unknown-symbol arm and no-match output, and the typed { variation exercises the shared sink/fountain symbol branch. recordings/cmd.c/lookaround-command.session.json reaches cmd.c dolookaround and produces the room plus doorway description through the canonical path, but it is not used as a new recording here. getpos.c getpos_menu remains an active caller entry with no matching recording; displayed glyph accessibility has no independent recording; later click/queued, lootabc, swallowed, hallucination, and multichar encyclopedia branches remain explicit caller gaps. No claim is made about an unmeasured later Knight boundary. Final source review confirms that hallucinated synthetic objects retain vague names through object_from_map, real OBJ_NAME entries use mksobj rather than mkobj, strange objects omit an article, and hallucinated monster naming suppresses the invisible prefix. Stored-glyph lookaround filtering precedes all naming, including squares with hidden live objects. The added getpos helper covers only GLOC_INTERESTING and its door predicate; no broader getpos completion is claimed. The rejected 41361354 candidate exposed rendered-byte and null-cell classification regressions. The correction uses canonical glyph identity and raw tty bytes for lookup, keeping encoded-prefix coordinates distinct; source-pinned display checks cover that contract. No broader display.c file completion is claimed.

callers.source: mklev.c makelevel() selects the special proto and calls makemaz(); js/mklev.js makelevel() resolves the current special-level loader and dispatches makemaz() at lines 657-737.
mkmaze.c makemaz() resolves the protofile and calls load_special(); js/mklev.js makemaz() invokes load_special(protofile, state) and performs the level-generation tail at lines 1805-1838.
sp_lev.c load_special() loads the Lua program through the des.* table and applies post-processing; js/mklev.js load_special() invokes the registered loader and special-level API at lines 1777-1802.
The production registry imports QUEST_LEVEL_LOADERS and spreads it into SPECIAL_LEVEL_LOADERS before makelevel dispatch.

functions.name: u_can_engrave
functions.sourceReview: Read the complete engrave.c:503-541 body. The function computes SURFACE_AT first; the swallowed-animal refusal precedes the swallowed-whirly floor message, while amorphous engulfers bypass terrain checks. The non-swallowed order is lava, pool or fountain, air, then !ACCESSIBLE. It then checks cantwield before check_capacity and returns the boolean result. The JS port preserves that branch and callback order, exact messages, and uses surface_typ() for SURFACE_AT. Direct callees are the is_animal/is_whirly macros, is_lava(), is_pool(), surface(), IS_FOUNTAIN, IS_AIR, ACCESSIBLE, cant_reach_floor(), cantwield(), and check_capacity(); each is already ported and none is replaced with note_unported(). The source function can emit text and surface() can draw through hallucinated hliquid(), so it is impure. engrave.c:doengrave() checks the returned false and returns ECMD_FAIL; js/engrave.js now does the same before any prompt.

result.summary: The v5 evaluation matches 34/45 screens, then stops at segment 0 step 34 when the Ranger selects a wished cursed scroll of teleportation with `r`, `g`. C accepts the scroll, reports that it disappears, and reaches the controlled level-teleport prompt on the next screen. `read.c:doread()` has no cursed-scroll rejection for a sighted hero; it calls `seffects()`, whose teleportation arm calls `level_tele()` for a cursed scroll. JS `read.js:doread()` rejects this valid case because `calmTeleport` requires an uncursed scroll and `confusedTeleport` only admits a blessed, noncursed scroll while confused. JS already has the cursed `seffect_teleportation()` → `level_tele()` arm, so the first missing branch is the `doread()` admission path. The remaining post-teleport movement and return-to-level inputs have not been replayed past this stop and are not claimed as matching evidence.

source.branch: A debug-mode Ranger wishes for a cursed teleportation scroll, then reads it while sighted and not confused. read.c:doread() passes the readable scroll through its generic scroll path; read.c:seffects() dispatches SCR_TELEPORTATION to seffect_teleportation(), which calls level_tele() because the scroll is cursed. The recipe then supplies level 2 at the controlled prompt. The saved C recording shows “As you read the scroll, it disappears.” at step 34, the level prompt at step 35, and “You materialize on a different level!” at step 37.
callers: cmd.c:1817 binds the `r` command to doread(). js/cmd.js:runReadCommand() calls js/read.js:doread(), and the `doread` dispatcher routes that result back through the command loop.
read.c:doread() obtains an object through getobj("read", read_ok, GETOBJ_PROMPT); C read_ok() suggests scrolls and spellbooks. The read-object selection prompt at case step 33 already matches.

read.c:doread() calls seffects(scroll) for ordinary scrolls and consumes its integer return to decide discovery and scroll cleanup. js/read.js currently calls its partial seffects() for the same source site.

read.c:seffects() dispatches SCR_TELEPORTATION to seffect_teleportation(&sobj); that helper chooses level_tele() for cursed or confused scrolls. The JS seffects() and seffect_teleportation() contain this source branch.
dependencies: For a whole doread() port, hack.c:check_capacity() returns the early ECMD_OK decision, invent.c:getobj() returns the selected scroll or cancellation, spell.c:study_book() returns whether reading spent a turn, and read.c:seffects() returns whether the scroll was consumed; those are all consumed return values. check_capacity(), getobj(), and study_book() already have JS implementations, but seffects() is explicitly partial and currently covers only a subset of read.c switch arms. The source-compliant whole-function scope must complete that return-valued seffects() dependency, not treat note_unported() as its result.

The selected seffects() arm calls read.c:seffect_teleportation(), a void helper. C read.c:2015-2032 and JS read.js:534-545 both route a cursed scroll to level_tele() and set gk.known; JS seffects() returns 0 so doread() retains responsibility for discovery and useup().

The selected level_tele() path is controlled because wizard mode is active: it consumes getlin() input "2", then consumes the boolean from apply.c:next_to_u() on the common tail before scheduling a goto. JS teleport.js has the corresponding call, and apply_next_to_u.js returns true for the case with no leashed companions or steed; its pet and mount branches remain explicit refusals, but are not reached by this recipe. The evaluation stops before JS executes level_tele(), so replay evidence is still needed.
The case continues with movement and an up-stairs command after arriving on level 2. Those later do.c movement/stair callers have not been diagnosed because the JS replay stops at the read branch.

functions.name: resist
functions.sourceReview: Read and compared the complete zap.c resist() definition at lines 6100-6158. The fake-player Conflict early return precedes all draws; attack level follows the exact class switch; defense level is capped at 50 or floored to the player level only for a monster player and otherwise to 1; then one rn2(100 + alev - dlev) comparison decides resistance. A resisted hit calls shieldeff_mon only when tell is true and rounds positive damage upward with (damage + 1) / 2. Damage is then subtracted, and lethal damage dispatches to monkilled(mtmp, "", AD_RBRE) only while gm.m_using is true, otherwise killed(mtmp); both calls discard their void result. The JS port preserves this order, uses the caller's RNG/environment bundle for death side effects, removes the former UnsupportedZapError refusal, and returns the resistance result. Existing killed/monkilled owners are invoked; no return-valued callee is substituted or skipped.
